Sports.title: Ex-Man United star responds to ‘confident’ Luke Littler’s dig at Lamine Yamal
Sports.content:
Patrice Evra has praised Luke Littler's confidence after the darts star compared himself to Lamine Yamal.

Former Manchester United and France left-back Evra was reacting to comments made by Littler, a die-hard Man United fan, about being the best 19-year-old in world sport.



2 Littler beat Gerwyn Price to win his second straight World Matchplay title Credit: Getty Images

After winning last month's World Matchplay, Littler told The Sun: "Obviously Spain won the World Cup and everyone is talking about Lamine Yamal.

"I mean he didn’t really do much, did he? Scored maybe one goal. Assisted, too.

"Is he the best 19-year-old in the world? No, he’s not!

"As long as I’m winning, playing well and picking up trophies, then that’s all that matters."



But Evra wasn't convinced it was necessarily a fair comparison.

"I need to see a picture," he said. " I don't like just the word athletes. When you say I'm the best in the world, I think every sport, it's different.

"And sometimes a Formula One driver can be better than a footballer if he's 19 years old. So it's difficult to compare. But I think it's the word athlete!



"I think his profession is not enough to be considered, you don't need to be an athlete in darts. Maybe to have the focus and everything. But doing darts, I can do many things to train for it! I don't know. I don't know. It depends on what we call a complete athlete."

But Evra admitted he respects Littler's belief in himself.

The five-time Premier League winner continued: "But if you feel that way, I mean, I love when people say that. I never say they are crazy. I never say they are arrogant. He's confident. If he thinks he's the best, let him think he's the best. What's the problem, guys?"



2 Evra starred in Man United's 2007/08 Champions League triumph Credit: Getty

Littler is the youngest world champion in darts history, winning his first PDC World Championship in 2025 aged just 17 and 347 days.

'The Nuke' went on to retain his crown at the 2026 World Championship and has already claimed five major titles this year.

With his World Matchplay success, the Warrington-born teenager became the first darts player ever to rack up £3million in prize money.



A lifelong Man United supporter, Littler paraded the World Championship trophy at Old Trafford following both his victories.

Back in 2024, he met legendary former manager Sir Alex Ferguson and captain Bruno Fernandes at a game against Tottenham, as well being presented with his own special shirt.

Man United are continuing their preparations for the new Premier League season – they get underway with a trip to newly promoted Hull on Saturday, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Hayden Panettiere's ex Wladimir Klitschko speaks out after star's death and vows to 'always speak of her with respect' to their daughter Kaya, 11
Sports.content:
Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko has spoken out for the first time since the star's death.

The actress, who passed away on Sunday, had her daughter with the boxer, 50. In 2018, when Kaya was three, she signed full custody to her ex amid her battle with postpartum depression and addiction and Wladimir moved their daughter to his native Ukraine.

A post-mortem examination showed there were 'no signs of trauma' - although her official cause of death, which came less than a week before her 37th birthday, is yet to be confirmed.

It was revealed on Monday that Narcan, a nasal spray used to rapidly reverse the effects of an opioid overdose, was found on a mattress in a loft apartment where Hayden died.

Naloxone, the active ingredient in Narcan Nasal Spray, blocks opioids like heroin, fentanyl, morphine and prescription painkillers from binding to brain receptors.

It allows the person to start breathing again within two to three minutes and stays active in the body for 30 to 90 minutes.

It is still unclear if Narcan had been used to try and revive Panettiere, although 911 audio obtained earlier on Monday revealed that the actress had gone into cardiac arrest following a suspected overdose.

Sharing a sweet snap of the family in happier times this morning, Wladimir wrote: 'Our family is going through a time of profound shock and grief...

'The announcement of Hayden’s tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya...

Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko has spoken out after the star's death

Sharing a sweet snap of the family in happier times, he added a caption reading: 'Our family is going through a time of profound shock and grief'

'She built an incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry. Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives...

'To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was...

'I extend my deepest condolences to Hayden’s parents, her friends, and her fans, who are also grieving today. Young and talented people like Hayden should not leave this world so soon...

'I ask everyone to please respect our family’s feelings and privacy during this incredibly difficult time. For now, this is all I wish to say...

'Thank you to everyone who is supporting my family and expressing their sincere condolences...

'Rest easy, Hayden. May you find eternal peace.'

Hayden and Wladimir met at a book launch in 2009. After two years of dating, they split up in 2011, before rekindling their relationship two years later.

Hayden and Wladimir met at a book launch in 2009. After they began dating, they split up in 2011, before rekindling their relationship two years later. Above, the couple in 2010

In October 2013, they were engaged, with the actress giving birth to their daughter, Kaya, the following December. However, it was confirmed in 2018 that the couple had split again but remained on amicable terms.

Later that year, Hayden announced she had made the 'difficult decision' to sign full custody of Kaya to Wladimir.

The widely-discussed move came after Hayden fell into a deep depression – which she said made her 'feel nothing' – and led to her 'turning to wine' and ultimately being sent to rehab for both depression and substance abuse.

In her final interview in May, she spoke to Dear Mome about her choice, saying: 'It wasn't a decision I made lightly, nor was it a decision I even wanted to make. I was going through a really challenging time in my life.'

The Heroes actress passed away on Sunday - just one week before her 37th birthday - with an autopsy showing there were 'no signs of trauma' although her official cause of death is yet to be confirmed

She told Jay Shetty on his On Purpose podcast in May: 'I have been the one who sought it out, who was saying, "I desperately need help. I know this is going to look terrible, but I am. I cannot live like this anymore..."

'The idea that anybody would think that I would just give away my child and be OK with it is heartbreaking. It couldn’t be further from the truth...

'It became this horrible cycle for years of battling depression and anxiety and alcoholism and substance abuse, and just me trying to find my way back.'

She added: 'I love my daughter, and I'm so proud of the young woman she is becoming. I talk to her all the time, and I feel so connected to her. She's like a mini-me.'

Discussing the prospect of bringing her daughter back, Hayden insisted that she would not want to take her away from her 'incredible' life in Ukraine.

She said, 'By the time I finally got healthy, I felt like it would have been unfair of me to, and selfish of me to try to pull her out of this life that she had been creating.'

The widely discussed decision came after she fell into a deep depression - which she said made her 'feel nothing' - and led to her 'turning to wine' and ultimately being sent to rehab for both depression and substance abuse

The star began acting as a child, appearing in soap operas then gaining wider recognition for her role in the 2000 sports drama Remember the Titans with Denzel Washington, and as the voice of Dot in Pixar's 1998 film A Bug's Life.

Hayden later found fame playing cheerleader Claire Bennet in the superhero drama Heroes before starring as country singer Juliette Barnes for six seasons on Nashville.

She earned two Golden Globe nominations for best supporting actress on the show, while her singing produced 11 entries on the US Billboard Hot Country Songs charts.

Hayden's film credits include 2006's Bring It On: All or Nothing, the comedy-drama film Raising Helen, and appearances in Scream 4 and Scream VI as Kirby Reed.

On Monday, Greenville County Sheriff's Office said that the post-mortem had been completed and that no signs of trauma were found on the star's body.

Further investigations will now take place to establish her cause of death, with chief deputy coroner Shelton England telling the Daily Mail that it was too early to discuss the drug overdose theory.

Meanwhile, a neighbor has spoken of the chaos that unfolded at the scene Sunday after Panettiere was found unresponsive and efforts to revive her proved unsuccessful.

Micah Lee, who lives in the Judson Mill Lofts complex where Panettiere died, claimed there was a 'bunch of commotion in the hallway' after the star allegedly 'collapsed' in a unit in the building.

'The halls are pretty hollow, so noise echoes throughout. And I had just heard about someone collapsing,' Lee told WYFF. 'And then afterwards there was talk about cardiac arrest. I can't confirm any of that. That's just what I've heard.'

The apartment block where Hayden was found in cardiac arrest in Greenville, South Carolina

In an audio of a 911 call made at 1.51pm Sunday, a female dispatcher described the actress as suffering a 'cardiac arrest.' A few moments later, a male dispatcher could be heard saying that she had suffered a suspected overdose at the home.

Hayden and her real estate agent ex-boyfriend Brian Hickerson were said to have flown from Los Angeles to South Carolina one day before she died.

Brian is originally from Greenville, public records show. It is unclear if the couple were in town to visit his family.

Her Nashville co-star Charles Esten also performed at The Foundry, a music venue inside the complex, on Friday night as part of his Carolina Tour.

Judson Mill Lofts is a former textile mill dating back to 1912, which was recently converted into apartments. These include studios and three-bedroom homes that can be rented from $1,295 to $3,485 a month.

Hayden and her real estate agent ex-boyfriend Brian Hickerson were said to have flown from Los Angeles to South Carolina one day before she died

Earlier, a representative for Hayden confirmed her death, saying her family would remember her as an 'incredible light' who brought 'immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her'.

A statement from her father, Skip, read: 'It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden.

'She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her - and to the millions who watched her onscreen.'

Her father also asked that her family be given privacy as they 'take time to process this unimaginable loss'.

Sports.title: New £18m Chelsea signing's girlfriend breaks down in tears as she reveals turmoil at prospect of leaving influencer career behind in Madrid to move to London
Sports.content:
Chelsea's new signing Pep Chavarria faces a difficult hurdle after his £18million arrival – his girlfriend is torn about moving to London.

The mysteriously named influencer Pawgli, who has been dating the footballer since November last year, broke down in tears in one video.

She says in other videos that she finds the prospect of moving to the English capital 'scary' and that she is 'panicking' over whether to relocate or not.

Pawgli has more than 1.1 million followers on TikTok and creates fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content for her audience.

Chavarria, 28, is in London for the foreseeable future after signing a five-year contract with the Blues, though they are hardly known for honouring long-term deals.

But Pawgli is weighing up whether she should join him or continue their relationship long-distance from Madrid, where her current influencer opportunities are.

Pawgli, the girlfriend of new Chelsea signing Pep Chavarria, is torn about moving to London

She broke down in tears, has described the situation as 'scary', and says she is 'panicking'

The duo have been together since November last year but she may decide to continue the relationship long-distance

She said: 'By moving to London, I'm kind of giving up on doing 100 per cent of my job. He has his job, I have mine; he earns his money, I earn mine. Nobody lives off anyone else; I don't live off my boyfriend.

'Therefore, by not living in Madrid, I'm losing opportunities - opportunities for me to keep growing in this - because absolutely everything is in Madrid.

'I want to keep holding on to my Spanish audience. I don't know how to speak English, at least right now, though I know I'll have to learn.

'But no matter how much English I know, I don't want to change my audience and have an English-speaking audience. I want to stay with my Spanish audience, which is why, all things considered, living in Madrid is so good for me.

'As someone who is ultra mega family-oriented and super sensitive, moving to a country I don't know, where I have nothing, no life, no job, and where I'm going to lose career opportunities...

'And I'm doing it out of love, because I love my partner and want to build a future and a family with him.'

Pawgli denied that she had broken down in tears over the prospect of losing work and going to free events in Madrid.

But in another video, she did clearly indicate that she is in some turmoil about the change.

Pawgli says she does not want to abandon her Spanish-speaking audience if she moves

The 27-year-old is 'mega-happy' for her partner but does not want to leave her family behind

Chavarria, a late bloomer who only made his LaLiga debut aged 24, has spent the last four seasons with Madrid-based club Rayo Vallecano.

Pawgli said: 'I have my life in Madrid; I have my job in Madrid, which luckily is going very, very well. I have projects, I have all the brands I work with there, I have daily events, I have my sister, my family, my friends. I have a life where I feel fortunate - it's a dream life for me and one that cost me a lot to build.

'So, when you start a relationship and your partner gets an opportunity like this, you're obviously ultra-mega happy for him and super proud of him, but you also have to sit down with yourself and think, "Okay, now what do I do?"

'And I swear until recently I was completely convinced that I wasn't going to move in with him. He has his life in London right now, I have mine in Madrid; I respect his life, he respects mine, and whenever possible, we'll see each other.

'A long-distance relationship. Something I would've never considered in my life, but if one thing was clear to me, it's that I will never in my life depend on anyone or live off anyone. I have my own income, and that's how it'll always be.

'All of this is scary for someone who has everything in Madrid. Right now I'm panicking, honestly, because I know it's a very tough decision.

'I also want to be able to experience this with Pep, because if I met my boyfriend and he's been here in Madrid for like 4 years and I met him, and precisely this year he has to go to London, maybe it's because fate also wants me to go.

'Because I'm obviously going to make content for you wherever I go, and being in London I can do even more, right? Because there are things there that aren't in Spain.

Pawgli, who has 1.1 million TikTok followers, insists that she wants a family with Chavarria

'I have a thousand ideas in my head because I can't stop thinking, honestly.'

Pawgli, 27, has never revealed her actual name and the nickname is apparently based off the Jungle Book character Mowgli.

She did join her boyfriend for his unveiling with the Blues.

Chavarria said: 'This is a dream for me as Chelsea are one of the biggest clubs in the world.

'It is a big opportunity but I am prepared and will work hard to help the team achieve success.

'There are a lot of people who have helped me get to this moment and I have to thank my family.

'They have always supported me and today is only possible because of them. I’m here thanks to Xabi (Alonso). For me, he’s one of the best coaches right now.'

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney names the Man United star Michael Carrick 'cannot rely on' - and reveals his fears for 'too small' midfield which will cost them in the Premier League this season
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney has named Luke Shaw as the player that Manchester United 'can't rely on' heading into the new season during the first episode of his new Red Devils-centric podcast.

Man United were downed by former manager Ruben Amorim's AC Milan 4-2 in their final pre-season friendly ahead of the start of the new Premier League season.

Their opening clash against Hull on Saturday will mark the first competitive match of Michael Carrick's tenure as permanent manager, but before the first ball is kicked, Rooney and his co-host of Stick to United Mark Goldbridge aired their concerns about Shaw's abilities - and whether the club might remedy issues in the transfer window.

'I thought Luke Shaw was at fault for all four goals,' YouTube star Goldbridge said. 'Thought we had a terrible game and I don't think he can play two games a week and then (Andrey) Santos goes off, you play (Youri) Tielemans and (Kobbie) Mainoo and there's no legs and there's no defensive capability.

'I sort of think, if I'm Michael Carrick, I'm light at left back, I'm light in the midfield.'

Rooney conceded that Shaw 'didn't have the best game', adding: 'I thought he had a really good season last season, but he didn't have the best game against AC Milan.

Wayne Rooney has suggested that Michael Carrick will not be able to 'rely' on Luke Shaw

The Man United veteran endured a tricky afternoon as the Premier League side lost to AC Milan

'So, I don't think you can rely on Luke Shaw to be consistent for the whole season.'

Instead, Rooney suggested that tempting Arsenal starlet Myles Lewis-Skelly to Old Trafford could provide a solution for Carrick.

'I know we're hearing that he's available for not much money,' Rooney continued. 'I think it's an absolute no-brainer.

'I think if you can get a player who can play left back, he can play centre midfield. He's young. He's got a massive future ahead of him. I think that's absolute no-brainer if you can bring him in.'

One situation which Lewis-Skelly would not be able to solve however would be Man United's robustness in midfield, with Rooney concerned that the physicality of Carrick's current crop could prove difficult.

'I don't know who this player is, but I'd like to see some physicality in the middle of the pitch,' he continued. 'A big box-to-box midfield player who can break up play, can drive with the ball, can see a pass, but ultimately he's got to be in that middle of the pitch and you've got that physicality.

'I think if you look at Tielemans, you look at Mainoo, you look at Santos, they're all small lads, there's not much pace among the three of them.'

Although Rooney was non-specific, he did suggest that Aston Villa's Amadou Onana could be 'that profile of player' that Man United need.

Carrick himself called for more signings last week as he rallied for the ownership group to put his squad in the strongest possible position for the new season.

'We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that,' Carrick said when asked about Man United's plan for signing players ahead of the September 1 deadline. 'Money's money, I get that.

'We feel like we have to be pushing for everything we're involved in, while being realistic of what the recent history's looked like over a period of time.

'For now, we've got to make the most of it, but we've got to push every boundary we can to be able to win again, basically. That's the challenge.'

Sports.title: Inside story of Aston Villa's summer: Why club dug heels in with Arsenal over Morgan Rogers, the Alejandro Garnacho loan explained, new £38m sponsor deals boosting the 'brand', the Villa Park revamp gamble and deals that could still be done
Sports.content:
Inside story of Aston Villa's summer: Why club dug heels in with Arsenal over Morgan Rogers, the Alejandro Garnacho loan explained, new £38m sponsor deals boosting the 'brand', the Villa Park revamp gamble and deals that could still be done

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Aston Villa may have lost several key men from their march to European glory but at least the guy who made it all happen is still in place.

Unai Emery is arguably the club’s greatest manager of modern times. He may not have won the league title like Ron Saunders or lifted the European Cup like Tony Barton, but in less than four years at the helm he has transformed Villa into a serious force – against substantial odds.

Villa dread the day Emery leaves and though there was never any serious possibility of him doing so this summer, there were a few jitters around the club’s Bodymoor Heath training ground last spring. When it appeared briefly that Diego Simeone and Atletico Madrid might part ways, Emery looked the ideal replacement.

His reputation in Spain remains very high, and Atletico’s director of football Mateu Alemany is a huge admirer. Alemany, remember, was on the point of becoming Villa’s president of football operations in spring 2023, only to back out at the last minute. One day, Simeone will leave Atletico and if Alemany is still in place, Emery will be high on his list.

Happily for Villa fans, they do not have to worry about that today. Yet what should have been a summer of celebration and consolidation turned into one of transition – as Emery always suspected it would.

Villa’s wrangles with UEFA financial rules have been discussed at length. This summer, it has meant one in, one out, with the £117million sale of Morgan Rogers driving the process.

Aston Villa may have lost several key men from their march to European glory but at least manager Unai Emery is still in place

The sale of Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for £117m has shaped the whole summer for Villa

Rogers’ record departure

Even when they agreed a new six-year deal with Rogers last November, Emery and his key lieutenants knew it would likely be their star attacker’s last season at Villa Park.

Villa were facing an uphill struggle to comply with UEFA spending rules and Rogers was the one asset able to ease those problems at a stroke. There was interest from across the Premier League and from Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich, too, but Rogers’ next club boiled down quickly to two: Arsenal or Chelsea.

The Gunners were the obvious choice. Newly-crowned Premier League champions and Champions League finalists, Mikel Arteta’s men were a hugely attractive option.

During England’s World Cup preparations, it is thought Rogers was sounded out by the Arsenal players in Thomas Tuchel’s squad. There were also discreet meetings between Rogers’ advisers and representatives working for Arsenal. The signs were positive.

Yet one thing was missing. While he was willing to let Rogers leave, Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris had studied the market and seen Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali given price tags of £100million and more. He was already irked by the idea that Arsenal might offer only £30million for Ezri Konsa when Villa value him at twice that. Why should he allow Rogers to leave on the cheap?

Arsenal had made Rogers their first choice but were unwilling to go above £80million, confident Rogers’ desire to join them would see the deal done in the end. How wrong they were.

It is unclear exactly when Chelsea sealed the Rogers deal but Daily Mail Sport has learned that at least a fortnight before the transfer was announced, the 24-year-old was very confident he would be heading to Stamford Bridge.

There are excellent relations between Sawiris and the leaders of BlueCo, who own Chelsea, and that undoubtedly helped the transfer and paved the way for Alejandro Garnacho to move to Villa Park on loan. Garnacho will join Villa permanently if he hits certain targets and could still be followed by Nicolas Jackson in the closing hours of the window.

Villa have a good relationship with Chelsea which paved the way for Alejandro Garnacho to move to Villa Park on loan

Could Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson be on his way to Villa too?

With Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne also leaving for Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, Villa are under no pressure to sell any more stars, though fringe players like Leon Bailey and – possibly – Tammy Abraham may leave.

Konsa’s future remains a doubt while there has been interest in Ollie Watkins, too, though neither would leave before high-level replacements are secured.

Zion Suzuki is set to join Villa from Parma for £30million and will become Villa's first-choice goalkeeper, despite Emi Martinez's move to Juventus collapsing.

Villa have taken a risk with Johan Manzambi. Buying any player while he is injured is far from ideal, certainly not for a £52million record fee. Manzambi’s knee injury, sustained at the World Cup, was significant and Villa must hope there are no lingering effects when he eventually returns to action.

Off the pitch

After Emery, the most important figure at Villa is Francesco Calvo. Operating with the rather grand title of ‘president of business operations’, the Italian’s job is to grow revenue. Fast.

The summer has been tough and the coming months promise to be equally challenging, though Calvo is working impressively.

By offering front-of-shirt space to new sponsors Visit Rwanda, where wealthier clubs were proposing only sleeve space, Calvo managed to win the race and secure a £20million-a-year investment – easily the largest in Villa’s history.

Arsenal received significant backlash for their sleeve partnership with Visit Rwanda, which ended in 2025, and Villa were braced for something similar. In June, the Democratic Republic of Congo filed a case against Rwanda at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), accusing its neighbour of breaching multiple international treaties.

Amnesty International have raised concerns yet compared with Arsenal’s deal, the reaction to Villa’s arrangement has been relatively mild.

Villa sealed a £20million-a-year sponsorship deal with Visit Rwanda, while last season’s front-of-shirt partner Betano will now have their name on the Villa sleeve

On top of the Visit Rwanda package, last season’s front-of-shirt partner Betano will now have their name displayed on the sleeve. That is worth an additional £18million over three years.

Apart from selling their best players, Villa’s only way to catch up with richer rivals is by improving their commercial status. Sustained improvement under Emery has made Villa a better ‘brand’, as the Spaniard put it ahead of the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain. Now the challenge is to bring more people through the door – another key item on Calvo’s to-do list.

New Villa Park

Formerly of Juventus and Barcelona, Calvo is ambitious. He is pushing ahead with a plan to increase Villa Park’s capacity to 50,000, starting from next season. The catch is that the North Stand will be closed this term, reducing the capacity to 37,000.

Trying to turn around a major building project in a little more than a year is brave. Liverpool needed nearly four years to complete the Anfield Road Stand. What happens if works run behind schedule, as they often do? Just ask anyone who has ever attempted even a minor renovation at home.

Emery has always had nagging fears about reduced capacity. The Villa boss was instrumental in shelving former CEO Christian Purslow’s redevelopment plans as he feared it would have too great an impact on home form.

If he is worried about it again, then he should look at Tottenham, who played at reduced capacity in their last season at White Hart Lane in 2016-17 and promptly won 17 of their 19 home games, drawing the other two.

Calvo is juggling numerous balls here. He is actively seeking a naming-rights deal but given the history behind Villa Park, must choose carefully. The North Stand project means 5,000 supporters will not sit in their usual seats this term.

Villa Park's North Stand will be closed this season, reducing capacity to 37,000 as the club try to increase the number of fans they can accommodate in the following season

On top of that, there is growing discontent about ticket prices and those voices may grow louder when the Champions League packages are announced.

Yet Calvo is in a tough spot here. Villa need to boost revenue and the temptation is to pull every lever to do so. There is a certain point, though, when fans will say ‘Enough’. The Villa Park atmosphere felt flat at times last season and that should worry everyone at the club.

If Calvo can emulate off the pitch what Emery has achieved on it, the future will stay rosy for Villa. It may prove an even more challenging job for the Italian than his colleague in the dugout.

Sports.title: Newcastle complete £29.5m signing of Amar Dedic as new Toon boss Matthias Jaissle reunites with former star: WINDOW WATCH

Newcastle complete £29.5m signing of Amar Dedic as new Toon boss Matthias Jaissle reunites with former star: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Liverpool being unlikely to pursue PSG star Ibrahim Mbaye - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Newcastle complete Dedic deal

Newcastle United have signed Bosnia and Herzegovina international Amar Dedic from Benfica for £29.5million on a five-year deal.

The 24-year-old full-back becomes the sixth senior addition of the summer and will wear the No 37 shirt at St James' Park.

Dedic, who can operate on either flank, previously worked with Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle at Red Bull Salzburg and Liefering.

He made 95 appearances for Salzburg before spells with Marseille and Benfica, where he featured against Newcastle in last season's Champions League.

Newcastle United have completed the signing of full back Amar Dedic

Dedic has won 31 caps for Bosnia and Herzegovina and played at this summer's World Cup.

'Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me. We know each other well. He knows what I can bring on the pitch and I'm really happy to be playing for him again,' he said.

'Playing Premier League football at St James' Park is going to be really special. Every game feels like a big occasion, with an amazing atmosphere. I'm really excited to get started.'

Owls target Anfield youngster

Liverpool winger Kieran Morrison is a prime target for Sheffield Wednesday on loan.

The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international has impressed during Liverpool's pre-season and has attracted varied interest from the likes of Wolfsburg and Bristol City.

However, League On Wednesday are emerging as strong favourites for his signature with Liverpool keen to see him get regular game time in a competitive division.

Morrison can play centrally in attacking midfield as well as wide. He joined Liverpool from Manchester United's academy and was called up to the Northern Irish senior squad for the first time, ahead of their World Cup qualifying play-off against Italy in March. He made his senior debut in June, playing the first half of a 1–0 friendly win over Guinea.

Liverpool are continuing negotiations for Paris St Germain winger Bradley Barcola but, as it stands, Liverpool are unlikely to pursue interest in his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye despite exploratory talks.

And elsewhere...

Aston Villa have agreed to loan right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic to Rangers with an obligation to buy for £3.5m.

Celtic also hold an interest in the Serbian international but he is expected for a medical at Ibrox later today.

Meanwhile, Brighton are keen on Millwall forward Femi Azeez, as Rangers continue to push for Amario Cozier-Dubbery, after their £7.5m bid was rejected on Monday.

Sports.title: Wales head coach Steve Tandy receives huge boost with Leicester Tigers coach set to join set-up ahead of Nations Championship campaign
Sports.content:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy receives huge boost with Leicester Tigers coach set to join set-up ahead of Nations Championship campaign

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leicester Tigers assistant coach Alex Davies is set to join Wales as a skills and kicking specialist in time for November’s Nations Championship campaign.

Wales head coach Steve Tandy is on the look-out for a new addition to his set-up to fulfil the role held for so many years by former No 10 great Neil Jenkins.

During Wales’ glory years under Warren Gatland’s guidance, Jenkins was a key figure behind the scenes.

He worked with the likes of Dan Biggar and Leigh Halfpenny during a golden era between 2008 and 2019 where Six Nations Grand Slams and Championship titles were commonplace for Wales.

Jenkins was immensely popular with Wales' players too.

He was a key part of the team which reached the 2019 World Cup semi-finals and briefly topped World Rugby’s rankings that year, while also working alongside Gatland in the same kicking role on four straight British & Irish Lions tours in 2009, 2013, 2017 and 2021.

Alex Davies (left) is set to join up with Wales in time for November’s Nations Championship campaign

Jenkins is still employed by the Welsh Rugby Union today and works with Wales’ academy and regional teams, but hasn’t been with the senior national team for the past 12 months.

In that time, former Wales backs Halfpenny and Rhys Patchell have both taken on the kicking coach role on an interim basis.

But Halfpenny has taken up a kicking and skills coach role with his former employers Cardiff while Patchell is now working with Italian club side Benetton alongside former Wales head coach Wayne Pivac.

It means the WRU has been keen to add a new, full-time employee.

Daily Mail Sport understands Davies – currently working at PREM Rugby side Leicester under their head coach Geoff Parling – will be that man.

The 40-year-old has previously worked with England Women, Rosslyn Park and the Netherlands after finishing his playing career with Bath in 2020.

His imminent appointment means he will join Tandy, Matt Sherratt, Danny Wilson, Peter Murchie, Dan Lydiate and Paul James on the Wales coaching staff.

It also comes at a time of continuing off-field upheaval for the Welsh game as the Welsh Rugby Union continues to try and move from four professional men’s teams to three.

Sports.title: Revealed: Jose Mourinho's four Real Madrid 'untouchables' - as Trent Alexander-Arnold faces battle to nail down right back spot
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho reportedly has four untouchable first-team starters at Real Madrid – but Trent Alexander-Arnold is not one of them.

Madrid begin their LaLiga campaign away at Espanyol on Saturday after a pre-season which has seen them go unbeaten.

They have bolstered their squad with six signings, including the £120million capture of winger Yan Diomande, who Liverpool had targeted, from RB Leipzig.

Los Blancos have also added Bernardo Silva and Ibrahima Konate for free and splashed out on Marc Cucurella, Carlos Espi, and Denzel Dumfries to take their total spend to around £205million.

Competition is hot, but Mourinho is reportedly implementing a 4-2-3-1 formation to accommodate his 'untouchables'.

Those four are the front quartet – Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham, Vinicius Junior, and Diomande – according to Spanish outlet AS.

Jose Mourinho reportedly has just four nailed-on starters with Real Madrid

Jude Bellingham is part of that quarter, which also includes Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, and Yan Diomande

It would suggest that Mourinho has a very defined idea of how he wants his team to attack and could be a departure from his typical pragmatism.

The rest of the squad find themselves in more of a battle and that is certainly the case for Alexander-Arnold, who will be competing with Dumfries.

Dumfries, also known for his prowess going forward, won two Serie A titles with Inter Milan and also reached two Champions League finals.

Alexander-Arnold has played two more minutes than him in pre-season (241 to 239), but some of Dumfries' have been on the wing.

At least he will not have to battle with former club captain Dani Carvajal, a fan favourite who left the club in May after 23 years with them across two spells.

Silva also finds himself in competition with Aurelien Tchouameni, Federico Valverde and Eduardo Camavinga for minutes.

The 32-year-old left Manchester City this summer after nine seasons and brings a different dimension to Madrid's midfield.

He has his work cut out to convince his manager, though, after Mourinho accused him of lacking fitness in their recent pre-season friendly against Ferencvaros.

Trent Alexander-Arnold will face fierce competition from newbie Denzel Dumfries at right-back

Mourinho is aiming to restore Madrid to glory after two disappointing seasons.

Madrid last won LaLiga and the Champions League in 2023-24 but have been outdone by Barcelona on the domestic stage and Paris Saint-Germain continentally.

Mourinho certainly brings the blockbuster factor and that much is evidenced in the fact he has a new Netflix documentary out.

But the 63-year-old Portuguese – who styled himself at Chelsea as a 'Special One' – has had a fallow past decade for the most part.

His last league title came with Chelsea in 2014-15 and despite reasonable success with Manchester United and Roma, he was unable to meet his high standards at Tottenham, Fenerbahce, and Benfica.

Sports.title: 8 blockbuster deals that could be completed in final two weeks of the transfer window
Sports.content:
The Premier League season may kick off this weekend, but none of its protagonists have completed their cast yet.

As is always the case, the football begins before the summer transfer window has concluded, creating a manic overlap for sporting directors, scouts, agents, managers and players.

Money is changing hands at a rapid rate, with a cumulative total of £2.14billion spent by the 20 Premier League clubs in the current window. With two weeks still to go, that is more than the £1.98bn total for the entire window in 2024.

It is being driven by inflated fees at the top end of the market, as well as increased outlay from the three sides promoted from the Championship, with both Coventry and Ipswich already surpassing £100m on transfers. But while much of their business has already been completed, there are some major deals which are still outstanding among the Big Six clubs.

‌



Here Mirror Football gives you a rundown of the main transfers which are in the pipeline and could be completed before the deadline on September 1.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Rodri to Barcelona

We start with an easy one. Manchester City have agreed to sell the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner to Barcelona for a fee which could reach £65m. Rodri has entered the final year of his contract with City and, having rebuffed efforts to sign a new one, made it clear he wanted out.

Barcelona are getting one of the world's best midfielders at a knocked-down price and the Premier League is losing one of its greatest ever players, albeit at the age of 30. An official announcement is expected in the coming days.

‌



Ayyoub Bouaddi to Man City

View 5 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi is poised to leave Lille for Manchester City (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/Getty Images)

City have wasted no time in securing their replacement for Rodri. With Tijjani Reijnders also heading to Saudi Arabian side Al Qadsiah for a fee of £51m, they are in need of reinforcements in the middle of the pitch and Bouaddi is their first port of call.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is valued at £85m by Lille and talks reached an advanced stage on Monday following the conclusion of the Rodri deal. Bouaddi is an exciting prospect, and despite £116m being spent on Elliot Anderson, he might not be the only one in the coming weeks.

Enzo Fernandez to Man City

Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez at Chelsea and wants the Argentina international to join him in Manchester. City missed the chance to trigger a £120m clause in his Chelsea contract, with the deadline passing on Friday, but the move could still happen.

‌



Fernandez was booed in Chelsea's final pre-season friendly of the season on the weekend and isn't exactly popular following Argentina's behaviour at the World Cup. He was suspended for two games by Liam Rosenior last season for publicly flirting with Real Madrid and, despite Chelsea's stance that they don't want to sell, the transfer has all the ingredients.

Bradley Barcola to Liverpool

View 5 Images Bradley Barcola is the No.1 target for Liverpool this summer (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

A contender for the biggest saga of the summer, Barcola could still end up playing at Anfield in the 2026/27 season. Liverpool have been biding their time, determined to wait for Paris Saint-Germain to lower their sky-high £145m asking price and there have been a few developments.

‌



Barcola has sat out of PSG's recent matches and a deal of around £110m to £120m could happen. PSG have signed forward Ferran Torres from Barcelona and winger Mika Godts from Ajax, paving the way for an exit. To make matters even more complicated, Liverpool are also interested in the French giants' 18-year-old star Ibrahim Mbaye.

Ezri Konsa to Arsenal

Arsenal need a central defender to help provide cover for the injured William Saliba and Konsa is their top target. The only issue is Aston Villa's £60m asking price, which is £20m more than Arsenal are willing to pay.

Bayer Leverkusen don't want to sell Jarrell Quansah and Atletico Madrid rejected an approach for Marc Pubill, leaving Konsa as the most likely candidate for Arsenal. Konsa has two years remaining on his Villa contract and, after a prominent role for England at the World Cup, is at the height of his value for Villa to consider a sale.

View 5 Images Ezri Konsa is Arsenal's most likely signing at centre-back (Image: Getty)

‌



Zion Suzuki to Aston Villa

Another interesting aspect at Villa concerns the goalkeeping department. For the second straight summer, Emi Martinez has been putting the feelers out to assess interest in a transfer away from Villa Park and the club have moved to sign Japan international Suzuki for £30m from Parma.

That deal is going ahead, so it remains to be seen what happens with Martinez who has put his cards on the table but is in limbo. The 33-year-old's move to Juventus collapsed over a fee and they have since agreed to sign Guglielmo Vicario from Tottenham instead, leaving the Argentina international with limited options.

Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa

View 5 Images Nicolas Jackson could leave Chelsea for £65m (Image: (Photo by Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images))

Chelsea have a frankly ridiculous number of players, some of which they desperately need to find new homes for in the coming few weeks. Jackson is one of the most valuable fringe players, with a £65m price tag after spending last season on loan at Bayern Munich.

‌



Villa are interested and have the funds, following the sales of Morgan Rogers, Donyell Malen, Youri Tielemans, Lewis Dobbin and Lucas Digne. It appears to be a good fit for both clubs and is one to watch in the coming weeks.

Savinho to Tottenham

Tottenham have been one of the biggest movers in the summer transfer window, splashing out to sign Mateus Fernandes, Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke after narrowly avoiding relegation. But they are not done yet: Spurs want a wide attacker.

Cody Gakpo is of interest to Tottenham, but there so far hasn't been any formal contact between Spurs and Liverpool. Savinho therefore appears to be a much more likely deal. The Brazilian winger is not wanted by Manchester City and talks have taken place over a deal, with the sticking point the fee. City initially quoted £85m for the 22-year-old - due mainly to the five years left on his contact - but that is sure to come down as time passes and negotiations continue for a player who has just seven goals and 16 assists in 84 appearances for the club.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd coach warns Michael Carrick his Old Trafford honeymoon could be over
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd coach warns Michael Carrick his Old Trafford honeymoon could be over

Former Man Utd coach Rene Meulensteen fears European football could prove a huge problem for Michael Carrick at Old Trafford this coming season

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has to face the demands of Champions League football this season

Michael Carrick has been told his honeymoon period as Manchester United boss could be over.

‌



Carrick worked wonders in the second half of last season after replacing the sacked Ruben Amorim on a caretaker basis. He engineered some seismic wins, to lead United to Champions League qualification.

‌



But Carrick has been warned that this achievement could come back to bite him this time round. Former United coach Rene Meulensteen reckons managing the increased workload of European football could lead to Carrick and his side's downfall.

‌



Meulensteen, who was No.1 to Sir Alex Ferguson at Old Trafford, said: "The number of games they're going to be playing is something completely different to last season.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Michael is going to have to manage the squad extremely well, because last season they played once a week and had plenty of time for recovery and probably more days off as well.

‌



"Whereas this season will be completely different as the volume of games, training sessions, and recovery days will change drastically. Not only that, but the travel time between games, especially playing in Europe, will have a huge impact as well.

"That's going to be something that United and Carrick have to come to terms with very quickly in the early stages of the season. Are they strong enough to handle it? If the squad stays the way it is currently, I doubt it."

View 2 Images Rene Meulensteen worked alongside Sir Alex Ferguson at Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Meulensteen also believes United's defensive consistency will be crucial if they are to cope with the demands of the season. He added: "I still think they're vulnerable at the back - and that's one thing Michael is going to have to sort out as soon as possible when the season starts.

"Finding a centre-back partnership that works, and getting some consistency in the back line will be key. Harry Maguire is coming off a good end to last season, but he needs some complimentary centre backs next to him.

"They have plenty of options at centre back in (Lisandro) Martinez, (Leny) Yoro, (Ayden) Heaven and even Luke Shaw can play in the position.

‌



"But the problem has been that inconsistency at the back, which he will need to sort out as soon as possible.”

Sports.title: Mount Blanc mayor tells 32 stranded mountaineers to pay for their own helicopter rescue
Sports.content:
Mount Blanc mayor tells 32 stranded mountaineers to pay for their own helicopter rescue

Mont Blanc mountaineers were told to foot the bill for their own rescue by the French authorities after rockfalls ensured the Gouter route was a dangerous proposition

View 2 Images Jean-Marc Peillex has been outspoken over funding rescues (Image: Philippe Lissac/Godong/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

A group of 32 mountaineers have been told to pay for their own helicopter rescue after becoming stranded on Mont Blanc. The mayor of Saint-Gervais, a village at the foot of the mountain, has accused the group of being 'dangerous' and demanded they foot the £2592 bill.

‌



There have been warnings over rockfalls that have emerged following droughts and heatwaves and made the Goûter route up Mont Blanc dangerous. Two refuges were closed on August 11 by Saint-Gervais leader Jean-Marc Peillex, due to the conditions available for climbers.

‌



A shelter warden called the day following that decision to indicate that a large group of climbers had started their ascent before the order was widely known. They are said to have discovered their fate at 3,835 meters after asking state rescue teams to helicopter them to safety

‌



Mountain rescue operations are typically free in France, but Peillex instructed private firm, Chamonix Mont Blanc Hélicoptères to bring them down at the cost of €95 (£81) per person. Some are said to have recoiled at the price and completed the 600-metre descent on foot without injury, according to Peillex.

"They deliberately refused to listen to the messages, recommending that people refrain from making the ascent or take into account the reality of the rockfalls, images of which were published on social media," Peillex said.

Gianni Infantino SACKS FIFA executive after criticism under-fire president READ MORE :

Emma Raducanu could QUIT tennis over injury hell, claims BBC icon READ MORE :

"It was therefore with full awareness that they climbed the Aiguille du Goûter, knowing that they would have to come back down. Everyone needs to understand that when the state pays for rescue operations, it is a blessed gift to insurance companies. It is time for this to end."

‌



Charles Van der Elst, chairman of the French Federation of Alpine and Mountain Clubs, defended the group and said Peillex was being misleading. The French mayor rejected Van der Elst's claims.

"The pointless controversy from [Van der Elst], completely out of touch and above all disconnected from the reality of the mountains," he said on X.

View 2 Images Helicopters are often used for rescues on Mont Blanc (Image: OLIVIER CHASSIGNOLE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Apparently, the climbers who got helicoptered back down look so proud of their stunt that they're bragging about it on Instagram," he added. "I did the right thing by charging them for the ride."

Peillex, who has long held such a stance, took his position after France's public spending watchdog recommended that foreign nationals should foot the bill for their own mountain rescues. Cour des Comptes recommended that this should be the case even when climbers have taken reasonable precautions.

‌



The Saint-Gervais mayor revealed in February that he agreed with such an approach and suggested that the number of foreign nationals requiring rescue on Mont Blanc accounted for about 60% of all cases.

"They don't pay taxes in France so why shouldn't they contribute to the cost?" he asked. "Free rescues give people the impression that they can do whatever they please with impunity.

"If emergency operations are needed because of a lack of preparation or proper equipment, they should be paid for by those who are rescued, not by the state or the local authority. Most people are insured but the state bears the cost instead of the insurance companies."

Sports.title: Sheffield United facing 'real prospect' of 12-point deduction in battle with ex-owner
Sports.content:
Sheffield United facing 'real prospect' of 12-point deduction in battle with ex-owner

Sheffield United's former owner Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is pursuing current owners Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen in court over alleged unpaid millions

View 2 Images Sheffield United's ex-owner Prince Abdullah bin Mosaad bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is behind the claims (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

Sheffield United's former owner claims the Championship club could be facing a 12-point deduction due to a row over money with the current owners.

Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud sold the Blades to Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen for just over £100million in December 2024. But now Prince Adbullah's company, United World, is attempting to wind up the company which bought the club.

It is claimed that COH Sports Bidco Ltd (CSBL) still owes £35m in missing installments for the purchase of the club. A hearing has been set at a London court on Wednesday.

"In short, they are trying to take the club without paying for it," United World said in a statement on Monday. In response, a spokesperson for the ownership group of Eltoukhy and Rosen described the petition as "a publicity stunt" and claimed the club is more “financially healthy” now than under his ownership.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

They also said they had invited the prince to “reinvest in the club and join the ownership of Sheffield United” again, adding that the co-owners “are focused on the sustainability of the club and the season ahead”.

The dispute centres around the decision to transfer Sheffield United’s shares from previous parent company CSBL to another one called 1919 Partners earlier this summer. Prince Abdullah claims that is an attempt to "avoid paying CSBL’s creditors".

United World said in a statement: "If the winding-up petition is granted on 19 August, as we expect, EFL Regulation 2.1.16 provides that Rosen must be disqualified from being a controlling owner and director of SUFC.

View 2 Images Sheffield United's current and former owner are in a financial dispute (Image: Maynard Manyowa/Getty Images)

"He will no longer be able to be chairman, or a director, he will no longer be able to exercise any control over the club and will have to sell a significant proportion of his controlling interest in the club.

"In addition, we understand that, once investigations are completed, there is a real prospect that the EFL may have to impose a 12-point deduction on SUFC under EFL Regulation 12.3, in order to 'protect the integrity and continuity of the League Competition' and 'the reputation of The League'."

United World have hired leading sports lawyer Nick De Marco and added: “As the former owners of SUFC, United World does not want to see SUFC facing months of uncertainty that will follow the winding-up order being granted on 19 August, but in the absence of Eltoukhy and Rosen, both billionaires, agreeing to pay what they owe, we have no alternative but to take all legal steps to protect our interests."

Article continues below

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire told BBC Radio Sheffield: "I think that (a winding up) is the worse-case scenario. Clearly United World are serious in the sense that they are entitled to be paid and the instalments that were due, there's no justification in those being missed by the new owners of Sheffield United."

"I've seen a lot of winding up orders relating to football clubs over the years. The vast majority are either settled on the court room steps before it goes into court, or the defending team will ask for some sort of postponement. I think it's unlikely that the company will be wound up on Wednesday."

Sports.title: Kyle Walker made Pep Guardiola cry during heated argument as Man City row emerges
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker made Pep Guardiola cry during heated argument as Man City row emerges

Kyle Walker captained Manchester City under Pep Guardiola but the pair had a heated bust-up in the dressing room in the defender's final City season

View 4 Images Kyle Walker and Pep Guardiola were involved in a fierce argument in December 2024 (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola's explosive bust-up with Kyle Walker left him fighting back tears, a new documentary has revealed. The pair had a huge row in the Anfield dressing room that eventually led to Walker's exit.

‌



After losing 2-0 to Liverpool in December 2024, Walker tore into his boss, fuming that he was being singled out for blame. The argument came just days after Guardiola signed a contract extension.

‌



“You keep saying my name, every meeting,” new footage shows Walker venting angrily. “Every f***ing meeting it’s my name.”

‌



When Guardiola suggested Walker’s name came up a lot because he’s a captain, the England international claimed “you didn’t want me to be a captain”. The right-back continued: “I’ve reacted to someone else, I’ve lost the ball, you somehow bring my name into it.”

The row between the pair features in a new four-part Prime Video documentary ‘A Beautiful Obsession’, which provides behind-the-scenes footage from Guardiola’s final two seasons as City manager. And, in response to Walker’s broadside, the Catalan coach struggled to hold it together while delivering an impassioned speech to his players.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Arsenal thump Man City to lay down early title marker and win Community Shield - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Inside Italy's talks with Pep Guardiola and real reason he snubbed job amid England links READ MORE :

“If I am a problem, you have to tell me,” Guardiola said. "I won’t stay here for the money or just for the fact of staying.

“I extended the contract because I want to be with you, I want to fight in that position. I don’t want you to feel like I’m leaving and running away from you.

“I don’t want to have the feeling that the pieces fall down. And I feel ‘No, I want to help you.’

‌



“But if you feel, captains first and then the other ones, that there is a problem? Tell me.

“It’s not going to change the love I have for all of you. Not one second. But I want to fight. That’s all. I’m sorry.”

View 4 Images The new documentary went behind the scenes of Guardiola's last two Man City seasons (Image: Prime Video)

‌



Watch Pep Guardiola doc A Beautiful Obsession for free This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £8.99 FREE Amazon Get Amazon Prime here Product Description Amazon Prime members can watch all four episodes of Pep Guardiola docuseries A Beautiful Obsession, which charts the former manager's final two seasons at Manchester City, for free when they launch on August 19.

Walker played just seven more matches for the club, three of them as captain, before joining AC Milan on loan for the second half of the 2024/25 season.

“Two days ago Kyle asked to explore the options to play abroad at the end of his career,” Guardiola said after leaving Walker out of his squad for an FA Cup match against Salford City in January 2025. “And for that reason I prefer to play other players whose mind is here.”

‌



The Treble winner left for good in the summer of 2025 after more than 300 City appearances, joining Burnley. Guardiola ultimately stayed at City until the end of the 2025/26 season, leaving one year before the expiry of his contract.

The manager's departure was officially announced before the final match of the campaign, days after a draw with Bournemouth saw the Manchester club admit defeat in the title race. He left having won six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five League Cups and one Champions League.

Guardiola hinted he would struggle to return to management after walking away. His final two seasons came against the backdrop of turmoil in his personal life.

‌



He split from wife Cristina Sierra in January 2025, though they have since begun to work towards a reconciliation. And Sierra was at Guardiola’s farewell match with their children, a gesture which he described as “so special to me”.

“It will be difficult to come back, that’s my feeling today,” he said after confirming he would leave. “I need to refresh many things that happened in my personal life and professional [life].

“What I’ve found, I need to find myself a little bit, in different things. Especially sitting and seeing time go by.”

‌



De Bruyne's tears

View 4 Images Kevin De Bruyne said his City exit was tough on his family (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Kevin De Bruyne fought back tears when he came to terms with leaving Manchester City. The Belgian midfielder won six Premier League titles with the club and was a key part of their Treble-winning squad in 2022/23 but his time at the Etihad Stadium came to an abrupt end after manager Pep Guardiola and City chiefs told him he would not be offered a contract extension.

“It’s really hard,” De Bruyne said in Guardiola's new documentary 'A Beautiful Obsession'. “My kids don’t want to go.

‌



“It’s been really stressful days and I’m not making decisions any more based on myself. It’s easy to go to another team and play football. But it’s been a tough time for us as a family.”

De Bruyne joined City from Wolfsburg in August 2015, playing one season under Manuel Pellegrini and nine under Guardiola. He is second on the all-time list of Premier League assist-makers and played his part as City won an unprecedented four league titles in a row under Guardiola.

City’s manager left 12 months later after adding two more trophies, the Carabao Cup and FA Cup in 2026. De Bruyne’s departure came as part of a plan to move towards younger players who can deliver for years to come.

‌



“We are going from a winning team that have been unbelievable [and] we have to create a new one,” City’s then director of football Txiki Begiristain said. “The [players] that made us the winners of everything, now they have to leave and we have to bring new people, new legs, new energy. Because if not, we won’t win.”

City have since spent money on younger talents including Rayan Cherki, who was 21 when he joined as De Bruyne’s successor. Begiristain also made way for a younger sporting director after 13 years, with Hugo Viana taking over.

And, in the first summer without Guardiola, the club broke their transfer record to sign 23-year-old England midfielder Elliot Anderson.

‌



Cherki convinced

View 4 Images Rayan Cherki quickly repaid Pep Guardiola's faith (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola ignored Rayan Cherki's red flags to force through his final statement signing. Cherki’s ‘chaotic’ reputation left Manchester City chiefs torn on whether he was the right man to replace Kevin De Bruyne.

Director of football Hugo Viana admitted the star’s off-field reputation set alarm bells ringing. But the playmaker bonded with Guardiola when the manager called him from his Manchester restaurant and the French international hit the ground running after earning the trust of the man he called the “best coach in the world”.

‌



Cherki starred for his country against Spain in the UEFA Nations League just days before signing for City. Guardiola joked that City CEO Ferran Soriano was grumpy because the Lyon-born star added £10million to his price tag with the performance but he insisted on the deal and Cherki joined for £34m in June 2025.

Cherki’s name came up as a potential replacement for De Bruyne when the Belgian left the Etihad Stadium. There were reservations over his mentality but Guardiola was eager to welcome him into the fold.

“The information on Cherki was not so positive,” Viana said. Soriano added: “Everybody knew about his abilities but there was this idea that he was chaotic.”

‌



However, the CEO later told chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak that checks from Viana and former sporting director Txiki Begiristain changed the club’s outlook. “There was one who gave a bad report but [from] when he was very young so they’re getting convinced that maybe his behaviour is just a myth.” Soriano said.

Cherki made an instant impact, scoring in the Club World Cup and adding a goal on his Premier League debut for City. He finished his first season in English football with 10 goals, 15 assists and two trophies - the FA Cup and Carabao Cup - and was one of the final signings of the Guardiola era before the manager left at the end of the 2025/26 campaign.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Bruno Fernandes bid incoming as Marcus Rashford to Barcelona still on
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Bruno Fernandes bid incoming as Marcus Rashford to Barcelona still on

Manchester United's Premier League season begins away at Hull City but there could still be some transfers completed before their opener

View 3 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has just four days until the new Premier League season begins (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have four days until their Premier League opener against Hull City. But Michael Carrick's squad has only been bolstered by three new arrivals thus far.

‌



In what has been Carrick's first pre-season at the helm, United have fared reasonably, winning two, losing two and drawing two. Their final friendly was against AC Milan and ex-manager Ruben Amorim, when they fell to a 4-2 defeat in Poland.

‌



Over the summer window, three senior additions have been made. Andrey Santos was signed from Chelsea for £50m, Karl Darlow joined after his Leeds United deal expired and Youri Tielemans arrived from Aston Villa for £35m.

‌



However, with less than two weeks left until the window shuts, major speculation surrounding Bruno Fernandes and Marcus Rashford is rife. Mirror Football brings you the latest out of Old Trafford.

Man Utd issue instant response to shock Bruno Fernandes transfer approach READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher says Man Utd won't win the title and names player they should have signed READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford U-turn

Rashford's future has been a topic of conversation throughout this summer transfer window after the English forward returned to United following a loan spell at Barcelona.

‌



View 3 Images Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and scored 14 goals (Image: Getty)

The 28-year-old played well in La Liga, but the Catalan giants opted not to make his loan move permanent for £26m, instead opting to sign Anthony Gordon from Newcastle for £70m and Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.

Rashford was left in limbo, with suggestions that he might be fully reintegrated at Old Trafford for the new season. However, new reports claim that Barcelona are not quite done.

‌



TEAMtalk claims they remain in contact with Rashford's representatives and despite making a series of attacking signings, continue to assess their options and could still attempt to pull off a dramatic return.

Rashford returned to United training on August 9 after starring for England at the World Cup. He played in their 4-2 defeat to AC Milan.

‌



Bruno Fernandes bid

In another shock revelation, United are braced for Galatasaray to mount a bid for captain Fernandes. In May, Mirror Football reported that the Portuguese playmaker would be a dream signing for the Turkish side.

Now, it appears they are doing all they can to entice him to Istanbul, with The Telegraph claiming they are ready to double his wages and offer £43m for Fernandes' services.

View 3 Images Fernandes has been linked with a move to Turkey (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

However, multiple outlets have suggested that United will swiftly reject the offer and any future bid, as they consider their skipper completely untouchable. His £55.6m release clause for foreign clubs expired in July.

BBC Sport specifically claims that Galatasaray would be wasting their time and that they are not the only club that might attempt to test United's resolve. Both Juventus and AC Milan have been suggested as potential interested parties. Fernandes' current contract expires in 2027, with the option to extend it by a further year.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Viktor Gyokores transfer offer as Premier League clubs eye Gunners star
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Viktor Gyokores transfer offer as Premier League clubs eye Gunners star

Arsenal are expected to make a huge sale shortly

View 2 Images Barcelona are reportedly preparing an offer for Viktor Gyokeres (Image: Getty )

Arsenal fans should hang on tight as the final two weeks of the summer transfer window are set to be an exhilarating ride. The Gunners showed that they are once more the favourites to lift the Premier League title this season by comprehensively beating Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield on Sunday.

‌



Their display showed how shrewd their summer signings have been, despite being rather understated compared to some of their rivals. Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes both started the fixture and impressed.

‌



More transfer activity in the form of new arrivals is expected before the window closes on September 1, with Mikel Arteta still wanting a versatile defender to fill in for the injured William Saliba, as well as a world-class forward.

‌



But sporting director Andrea Berta deems it necessary to first offload several players in order to raise funds and free up squad space. With Leandro Trossard being the only major departure of the summer, the north Londoners are set to ramp up their dealings over potential exits before turning their attention back to signing players.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal handed unanimous Premier League title verdict after thumping Man City READ MORE :

Raheem Sterling spotted working different job as search continues to find club READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer developments concerning the Premier League champions.

‌



Gyokeres offer 'imminent'

Spanish outlet Sport has reported that Barcelona are preparing to make an offer for Arsenal’s Viktor Gyokeres 'imminently'. The La Liga champions are searching for a forward to replace Ferran Torres after the World Cup winner joined Paris Saint-Germain for £43m.

Barcelona’s first choice target is Julian Alvarez - also admired at Arsenal - but Atletico Madrid are refusing to sell the Argentine to a direct rival. As such, Barca have reportedly turned their attention to Gyokeres.

The report claimed that Barcelona would test the waters at the Emirates Stadium and "make movements in the next few hours". The Swede joined Arsenal last summer in a deal worth up to £64m and was tipped to finally end Arteta’s long search for a goal-scoring No.9.

‌



But despite scoring 21 goals in all competitions in his first campaign for the Gunners, Gyokeres’ all-around play left a lot to be desired and he often went missing in important games. That led to rumours of his potential exit earlier this summer, with previous reports claiming Arsenal were willing to offer Gyokeres in a player-plus-cash deal for Alvarez.

Rivals circling for Nwaneri

View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri is likely to depart north London this summer (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

‌



Fabrizio Romano dropped a bombshell during Arsenal’s win over City on Sunday by claiming the decision has already been made for Ethan Nwaneri to leave the Gunners in the next two weeks. He wrote on X that the club made the decision weeks ago to let the 19-year-old, who was sent out on loan for the second half of last season, depart.

That came after Nwaneri did not even make the bench for the Community Shield clash. The versatile youngster was seen watching on from the sidelines with Gabriel Martinelli, another player heavily linked with a move away this summer, as their team-mates took part in the Principality Stadium trophy celebrations

Romano has since doubled down by claiming several clubs have already approached Arsenal over a possible deal for Nwaneri, including AC Milan, Galatasaray and unnamed German sides. He went on to say on his YouTube channel that there is a feeling at Arsenal that Premier League clubs are now expected to join the race for his signature.

Article continues below

Nwaneri is said to be conferring with his agents and family before making a decision regarding his next move following a poor loan stint with Marseille last term.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
